statement: Parametric attaining theorem and matching method barrier. If 2/5<theta<3/5 satisfies the source paper's short-prime count PI(theta), then for every fixed c<(1-theta)/3 and all sufficiently large k, every integer 2k<n<=exp(c(log k)^2/loglog k) has a prime divisor p in (k,k+3k^theta) of (n-k)...(n-1), hence p in (k,2k). With the Baker--Harman--Pintz value theta=21/40, this gives every c<19/120. Conversely, no termwise blockwise Theorem 4.1 little-o certificate as precisely defined in evidence/parametric_frontier_proof.md reaches c>=(1-theta)/3; this no-go is about that certificate class, not the true bad-point count or Erdős #451 as a whole.
